- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) or volatile, model often overpredicts; reduce forecast to reflect bearish or uncertain sentiment.  
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5–10% in 1–2 days); apply a 1–2 day lag correction to smooth out overreaction.  
- In mean-reversion scenarios (e.g., price near 60–65 after prolonged volatility), model tends to hold too low; adjust upward by 1–3% to capture reversion bias.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model underestimates true price in early periods (e.g., first 5–7 days) when sentiment is neutral or mildly bullish; apply a 0.5–1.5% upward bias for early horizon.  
- When sentiment history shows repeated low values (e.g., 0.00–0.27), model often fails to recognize support levels; add a floor correction at 5–10% below recent low.
